subject: Clarify: model improvement opt-outs, evidence & DPA redline
messages:
From: Claire Brooks <claire@averyhealth.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@averyhealth.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions: model improvement opt-outs & DPA evidence

Diego,

Thanks for taking the call earlier. As we move toward legal review, Avery has a few tightly scoped asks so we can keep the pilot internal-only and eligible for our healthcare compliance program. High level: we need a clear 'no-training' commitment for our production data by default, plus an operational evidence package showing how Redwood enforces that with subprocessors and cross-border transfers. Specifically:

- Can Redwood confirm "no-training" on Avery data unless we opt in in writing?
- What derivative rights does Redwood retain (if any) for telemetry, aggregated metrics, or model improvement? We need explicit wording that customer prompt + response are not used to improve models in a way that would make outputs available to others.
- Can you provide a sample evidence manifest (ops artifacts) you would produce for SOC/internal audit (subprocessor inventory, datapath diagrams, KMS residency, proof-of-deletion timelines)?
- We will send a redline to your DPA — can you confirm typical turnaround for first-pass and whether Redwood is open to onshore KMS or on-prem keys for our EU/US residency requirements?

Attached: Avery_DPA_questions.pdf (list of clause references). Please include any standard attestation we can share with our security reviewers. Procurement is looped for contract timing.

Best,
Claire Brooks
Legal Ops | Avery Health

--
Attachment: Avery_DPA_questions.pdf (1 page, PDF stub)

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: Claire Brooks <claire@averyhealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions: model improvement opt-outs & DPA evidence

Claire — thanks for the clear list. Short answers first, then details and what we can include in an attestation pack.

TL;DR:
- No-training by default: Yes, we can commit to not using Avery production data to train, fine-tune, or update public/shared models unless you explicitly opt in via contractual amendment and signed SOW.
- Derivative usage: Redwood requires a narrow internal license to aggregate anonymized telemetry and model metrics strictly for service reliability and safety (e.g., anomaly detection, model drift monitoring). We do not use prompt/response content to retrain models that would make customer outputs available to others. We can commit to a clause that derivatives are for internal engineering/ops only and not for model marketplace or licensing.
- Evidence manifest: we can provide an "Operational Attestation Package" including: subprocessor inventory + last-audit dates, dataflow diagrams for request/response and ephemeral KV stores, KMS residency/keys used (cloud region), retention/deletion proof (logs of deletion requests), and a short runbook of how we enforce no-train paths (prefix/KV tagging, routing to dedicated pools).

What I'll attach: redwood-no-train-explain.pdf (short explainer) and a proposed_operational_attestation_outline.docx you can share with security. If you send the DPA redline we'll do a first-pass review within 3 business days and flag any non-standard asks. Onshore KMS: we support customer-managed KMS + dedicated-routing for residency (we'll need procurement/legal to sign a SOW for dedicated keys or Dedicated/Private deployment options — happy to outline options).

Next steps I propose:
1) You send DPA redline; we produce a marked-up version + an operational attestation draft.
2) We prepare an evidence sample (anonymized) showing subprocessor list + a small dataflow diagram.
3) If Avery needs on-prem KMS or dedicated keys, I'll loop Solutions Eng to scope the SOW.

Happy to jump on a 30-min follow-up with your security engineer next week.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Lead, Enterprise Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: redwood-no-train-explain.pdf (2 pages), proposed_operational_attestation_outline.docx (outline)

From: Claire Brooks <claire@averyhealth.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@averyhealth.com
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Questions: model improvement opt-outs & DPA evidence

Diego — appreciate the quick reply and the outline. I've attached our DPA redline (Avery_DPA_redline.docx) — highlights:

- Section 4.2 (Use of Data): we propose explicit language: "Customer Data will not be used to improve, retrain, or otherwise modify any machine learning models without Customer's separate written consent."
- Section 6.1 (Subprocessors): request a 30-day notice period before onboarding a new subprocessor and a right to object for high-risk subprocessors.
- Section 8.3 (KMS/Residency): we'd like confirmation that keys can be customer-managed and mention onshore (US) residency for certain datasets; please advise how Dedicated/Private vs Hosted options differ here.
- Evidence: procurement asked for a sample timeline for producing the Operational Attestation Package (we need it within two weeks of contract signature ideally).

We're targeting a Q2 sign-off cycle; procurement flagged any SOW or fee for dedicated key handling upfront. Sending redline now.

Claire

--
Attachment: Avery_DPA_redline.docx (redline, 3 pages)

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 29 May 2027 18:03:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Questions: model improvement opt-outs & DPA evidence

Forwarding Avery's DPA redline and asks. Key points & suggested responses below.

On 2027-05-29 09:18 -0400 Claire Brooks <claire@averyhealth.com> wrote:
> Diego — appreciate the quick reply and the outline. I've attached our DPA redline...

Internal notes (inline):
- No-training clause: I recommend we agree to the explicit line Claire proposes for customer production data. That aligns with our standard "no-train by default" offering and will remove a major procurement blocker. Legal: can we sign to "not use to improve, retrain, or otherwise modify any ML models without Customer's separate written consent"?
- Subprocessors / 30-day notice: operationally we already publish a subprocessor list; 30-day notice is reasonable for major changes but we should push back on an absolute objection right (propose: objection right for high-risk processors with documented mitigation plan).
- KMS / Residency: options: (A) Hosted + customer-managed KMS (no extra fee but limited to cloud-provider KM options), (B) Dedicated routing + enforce onshore regions (may require Dedicated/Private deployment SOW), (C) On-prem key integration (SOW + engineering effort). Need Product + Sales to estimate timeline and any procurement fee.
- Evidence timeline: two-week turnaround after signature for an attestation pack is aggressive but feasible for a limited artifact set (inventory + diagram + deletion samples). We should offer a 10-business-day SLA in the SOW for the initial pack and 30 days for any expanded artifacts.

Action items:
1) Kimberly — legal check on acceptability of the exact no-train language (and whether we need any carveouts for safety/testing).
2) Jordan — can you estimate engineering effort / SOW cost to support customer-managed KMS vs Dedicated routing? Also estimate time to produce a redacted evidence sample for procurement.
3) I'll draft the initial attestation outline based on the attached template and prepare the first-pass responses to the DPA redline.

Thanks — Diego
